mainTopic: When an error on שבת is excused because שבת 'stands to be overridden' (נתנה שבת לדחות): applying the מילה case to קרבן ציבור, רב אשי's challenge, and opening a new question on the משנה about other זבחים slaughtered לשם פסח
overview: This amud opens by finishing an explanation of the מילה case: a mistake on שבת is excused only if שבת was set to be overridden for this particular person, and רב כהנא defends this against רב אשי's challenge. The גמרא then shows that our משנה, which divides between animals fit and unfit for a פסח, follows רבי שמעון, while רבי מאיר exempts in every case. It explores how far רבי מאיר goes: he exempts even a calf of שלמים and even חולין, but not בעלי מומין. רב נחמן explains that he exempts if the person was busy with a קרבן or if the animal could easily be mixed up. Next, ריש לקיש rules that someone who ate נותר thinking it was roasted קרבן meat is liable. רבי יוחנן rules that relations with one's wife who is a נדה make a man liable, but with one's יבמה he is exempt, and the גמרא narrows the wife case step by step until the difference holds. The גמרא then searches for a תנא who agrees with רבי יוחנן, but each source (לולב, זבחים, babies, תרומה) is rejected because its מצוה is time-pressured. The תרומה case is also rejected because eating תרומה counts as עבודה. The amud ends with the story of רבי טרפון, which proves that eating תרומה is called עבודה; the פסוק comes on the next amud.

steps.title: First clause versus last clause: was שבת set to be overridden?
steps.stepSummary: The explanation ends here. In the רישא of the מילה case, שבת was not set to be overridden, so he is liable. In the סיפא, שבת was set to be overridden for him, so his error is excusable.
steps.simpleTranslation: [In the first case he is liable] because שבת was not set up to be overridden. [But in the last case, שבת was set up to be overridden for him.]
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the two cases of mistaken מילה on שבת are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the baby whose מילה belonged on שבת had already been circumcised. Nothing left that day could override שבת, so circumcising the other baby was a plain mistake, and he is liable. In the סיפא, there was still a baby whose מילה overrides שבת. Because שבת was 'open' to be overridden for him, his confusion is treated as an excusable error.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת was 'given' (set up) to be overridden: it stands open to being pushed aside for this מצוה
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
For him / with regard to him

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The first words, 'that Shabbat was not given to be overridden', are the reason for the first case (רישא) of the מילה law, which was mentioned on the previous amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: The test 'was שבת set to be overridden?' becomes the key tool for the rest of this discussion.

phrases.english: for Shabbat was not given to be overridden.
phrases.notes: This is why he is liable in the first case (the רישא).

phrases.english: [But the last clause: Shabbat was given to be overridden for him.]
phrases.notes: This is why he is exempt in the last case (the סיפא), according to רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two cases by a single principle: whether שבת stood to be overridden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think both מילה mistakes should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability depends on whether שבת was set to be overridden for him at that moment.

steps.title: Applying the principle to communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The same principle explains our case. שבת is overridden for קרבן ציבור, so someone who slaughtered for that purpose by mistake is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, שבת was set up to be overridden for a communal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the rule from the מילה case and applies it to slaughtering on שבת for the sake of a קרבן ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבנות ציבור are brought on שבת, so שבת is 'open' to be overridden for them. Someone who mistakenly slaughtered other offerings for that purpose had a reasonable basis for his error, just like the סיפא of מילה. Therefore he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, meaning our case
Behold / after all
Communal offering brought on behalf of all Israel (such as the תמיד and מוספין), which overrides שבת

phrases.english: Here, after all, Shabbat was given
phrases.notes: Turning back to our case.

phrases.english: to be overridden for a communal offering.
phrases.notes: So the mistake is excusable, and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 1 to the case of קרבן ציבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone who slaughters on שבת for the sake of a קרבן ציבור is exempt, because שבת is overridden for such offerings.

steps.title: רב אשי: שבת is overridden for babies in general
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב כהנא. In the רישא of מילה, שבת is also overridden for babies in general, so why is the man liable there?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: Here too, שבת was set up to be overridden for babies in general!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the principle. If 'general' overriding counts for קרבן ציבור, it should also count for מילה, which overrides שבת for babies everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 counted קרבן ציבור as a general category that overrides שבת. מילה on the eighth day is also a general category that overrides שבת for all babies. So by that logic, even the רישא should be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Late Babylonian אמורא, a main editor of the Talmud Bavli
Babylonian אמורא; here the one defending the explanation
Here too, the same logic applies
Babies in general (other people's babies)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how consistently the principle from steps 1 and 2 is applied.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא of מילה is a case where 'שבת was not given to be overridden.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If general overriding (as with קרבן ציבור) is enough, then מילה, which overrides שבת for babies in general, should also make the רישא exempt.

steps.title: רב כהנא: for this particular man, it was not given
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that what matters in מילה is whether שבת was overridden for this person. For him, it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As far as this man is concerned, at least, it was not given.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge. In מילה, we look at the specific person, not at babies in the world in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא admits that שבת is overridden for babies in general. However, this man had no baby left whose מילה belonged on שבת, so for him personally nothing overrode שבת. His mistake therefore has no basis. In the case of קרבן ציבור, by contrast, the communal offerings do override שבת on that very day.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to
This man
At least, in any case
It was not given

steps.whatToRemember: The test is not only whether שבת is overridden 'in the world'. In the מילה case, the question is whether שבת was set to be overridden for this specific person at that moment.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.english: with regard to this man, at least,

phrases.notes: שבת was not set to be overridden for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: individual versus general
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי thought general overriding for all babies should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: In מילה, the relevant overriding is personal. This man had no Shabbat-day מילה left, so he is liable.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on other offerings slaughtered for a פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה. If someone slaughtered other זבחים on שבת לשם פסח, he is liable if they are unfit for a פסח. If they are fit, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all other offerings that he slaughtered for the sake of a פסח: if they are not fit, he is liable; if they are fit, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new section by quoting a line of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה splits the case in two. Animals that could never serve as a פסח (unfit) bring definite liability. Animals that could be a פסח (fit, such as a male lamb in its first year) are the subject of a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. This split between fit and unfit is what the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals / offerings
For the sake of (with the intent of) a פסח offering
Fit, meaning animals that could qualify as a פסח
Sin-offering brought for an accidental transgression
Exempts

phrases.notes: The משנה makes it sound like רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree here, but רבי מאיר exempts even this, as Step 7 shows.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רְאוּיִין — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּיב חַטָּאת,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfit animals: liable. Fit animals: מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר (liable) and רבי יהושע (exempt).

steps.title: Which תנא distinguishes between fit and unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the law depends on whether the animals are fit for a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא that distinguishes between fit and unfit animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's split between fit and unfit animals, opening a new investigation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה assumes that fitness matters. The גמרא wants to identify which תנא holds this view, since not every opinion would draw this line. The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose opinion is this)?
Who distinguishes / for whom it makes a difference

phrases.english: Who is the tanna that distinguishes
phrases.notes: The גמרא wants to know whose opinion this is.

phrases.english: between fit ones and unfit ones?
phrases.notes: The answer comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּשָׁנֵי לֵיהּ בֵּין רְאוּיִין לְשֶׁאֵינָן רְאוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the distinction the משנה just made in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that fitness for a פסח affects liability.

steps.title: Our משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The anonymous view of the משנה is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר exempts in every case, while רבי שמעון splits between fit and unfit animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא teaches: whether the animals were fit or unfit for a פסח, and also if he slaughtered for the purpose of communal offerings, he is exempt. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי שמעון says: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree he is liable for unfit animals. They only argue about fit animals. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. The משנה follows רבי שמעון, and a ברייתא proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר exempts no matter what, whether the animals were fit or unfit. Only רבי שמעון makes the law depend on fitness, just like our משנה. So the משנה must follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
Fit (here: animals fit to be a פסח)
Communal offerings
Exempt (no חטאת needed)
Sin-offering brought for an accidental sin

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר always exempts. רבי שמעון makes the law depend on whether the animals are fit for a פסח, and our משנה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon.
As it was taught: whether the offerings are fit
or the offerings are not fit,
and likewise one who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings —
he is exempt; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree
about unfit ones, that he is liable;
about what did they disagree? About the fit ones,
that Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון. רבי מאיר exempts even for unfit animals.

steps.title: רבי מאיר exempts even for a calf
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי, quoting רבי אלעזר, says רבי מאיר exempts even someone who slaughtered a calf of שלמים for the sake of a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר: רבי מאיר exempted even a calf of שלמים that he slaughtered for the sake of a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explores how far רבי מאיר's exemption reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be a lamb or a kid, never a calf. Even so, רבי מאיר exempts this person. The mistake is a big one, yet it still counts as an error made while trying to do a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Calf
Peace-offerings
For the sake of the פסח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Meir would exempt
even a calf of peace-offerings
that he slaughtered for the sake of the Paschal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on רבי מאיר's view from the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר exempts even when a calf of שלמים was slaughtered as a פסח.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges from blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects. רבי יוחנן said that רבי מאיר agrees a person is liable for בעלי מומין, so why not for a calf, which is also totally unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב ביבי: But didn't רבי יוחנן say that רבי מאיר agreed regarding blemished animals?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רב ביבי's broad reading of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר holds a person liable for animals that could never be offered, such as בעלי מומין, then a calf should be the same. A calf can never be a פסח either.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (introduces a challenge)
Agrees / concedes
Blemished animals

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב בִּיבִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Beivai:
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין!
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir conceded regarding blemished animals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי's claim that רבי מאיר exempts even for a calf
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unfit animals (בעלי מומין) make him liable, and a calf is also unfit for a פסח.

steps.title: A calf keeps him busy, blemished animals do not
steps.stepSummary: A person pays no attention to בעלי מומין because he knows they are out. A calf he is actively busy with as a קרבן, so a mistake there is understandable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: With blemished animals, he is not busy with them. But this one, he is busy with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי answers by showing that a calf and a blemished animal are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's exemption needs the person to have been busy with the מצוה when he erred. A שלמים calf is a real קרבן that he is handling, so he can get confused. A blemished animal is ignored completely, so there is no excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: Busy / preoccupied
He is not preoccupied with them

phrases.english: He said to him:
With blemished animals, he is not preoccupied with them,
but this one, he is preoccupied with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal that can never be a פסח makes him liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether he was busy with the animal as a קרבן. A calf yes, a blemished animal no.

steps.title: רבא asks about unconsecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what רבי מאיר would say about someone who slaughtered חולין for the sake of a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Someone who slaughtered חולין for the sake of a פסח, what would רבי מאיר say?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question tests רבי מאיר's exemption with a case that goes even further: a regular, non-holy animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf of שלמים is at least a קרבן. חולין is not holy at all. So רבא wants to know whether the exemption still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
Unconsecrated (ordinary) animals

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Naḥman:
Unconsecrated animals for the sake of a Paschal offering,
what would Rabbi Meir say to me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a parallel, more extreme case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי מאיר exempt someone who slaughtered חולין as a פסח?

steps.title: רבי מאיר exempts even unconsecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבי מאיר exempts even when חולין were slaughtered for the sake of a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי מאיר exempted even חולין for the sake of a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a clear answer: yes, the exemption covers even חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This stretches רבי מאיר's exemption to its widest point. Even an animal with no holiness at all is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rabbi Meir would exempt
even unconsecrated animals for the sake of a Paschal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹטֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲפִילּוּ חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר exempts even for חולין.

steps.title: Challenge again from blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects. If רבי מאיר holds a person liable for בעלי מומין, which can never be offered, then חולין should also make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say that רבי מאיר agreed regarding blemished animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge from רבי יוחנן is now aimed at רב נחמן's ruling about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer from Step 10 does not work. A person is not busy with חולין as a קרבן either. So a new answer is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: This uses the same words as Step 9, but it is a separate challenge against a different ruling (חולין, not a calf). The answer will also be different.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין!
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir conceded regarding blemished animals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that רבי מאיר exempts for חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חולין, like בעלי מומין, can never be offered, so he should be liable.

steps.title: Unconsecrated animals can be confused, blemished ones cannot
steps.stepSummary: A blemish is visible, so no one mixes up a blemished animal with a kosher קרבן. חולין look exactly like קדשים, so a mix-up is understandable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blemished animals are not confused. These are confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered with a new distinction, based on how easy it is to mix the animals up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר exempts when the error is a reasonable one. חולין look identical to holy animals, so the mistake makes sense. A blemish is obvious, so there is no excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: They get confused / mixed up
These

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר exempts when the error is understandable: when he was busy with the animal as a קרבן (a calf), or when it looks like a קרבן (חולין). He holds a person liable for בעלי מומין, since neither reason applies.

phrases.english: Blemished animals are not confused,
these are confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal that can never be offered makes him liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: חולין look like קדשים, so the mistake is reasonable. Blemished animals are clearly different.

steps.title: Is the reason really a mix-up, or is it being busy?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the mix-up reason. רב ביבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר that רבי מאיר exempts even a calf of שלמים slaughtered for a פסח. A calf can never be mistaken for a פסח, so רבי מאיר's reason must be that the person was busy with a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי מאיר's reason really that some animals can be mixed up and others cannot? But רב ביבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר that רבי מאיר exempts even a calf of שלמים slaughtered for the sake of a פסח. So it seems that רבי מאיר's reason is that the person was busy with a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer רב נחמן just gave. He brings a teaching that seems to show רבי מאיר's real reason is not a mix-up but being busy with a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf can never be a פסח, since a פסח must be a lamb or a goat, so nobody could mix the two up. Yet רבי מאיר still exempts. That suggests his reason is 'being busy with a קרבן.' If so, plain חולין, which a person is not busy offering, should make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Being mixed up or confused (one thing mistaken for another)
A calf, which can never be used as a פסח
Peace-offerings
Evidently / this shows that
Busy, preoccupied

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that a פסח can only be a lamb or a goat. That is why a calf can never be confused with a פסח, and it is the whole force of רבא's question.

phrases.english: And is the reason of Rabbi Meir
because these get confused and those do not get confused?
phrases.notes: This refers to רב נחמן's answer in Step 14.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Beivai say that Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Meir would exempt
even a calf of a peace-offering
that he slaughtered for the sake of the Pesach!
phrases.notes: A calf can never be a פסח, so there is no possible mix-up.

phrases.english: Evidently, Rabbi Meir's reason
is because he is busy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם אִיחַלּוֹפֵי וְלָא אִיחַלּוֹפֵי? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the mix-up reason given in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that רבי מאיר's reason is the likelihood of a mix-up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר exempts a calf, which cannot be mixed up with a פסח. So his reason must be being busy with a קרבן, and חולין, which a person is not busy offering, should not be exempt.

steps.title: Two separate reasons, and either one is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבי מאיר exempts for either reason. Being busy exempts even without a possible mix-up, and a possible mix-up exempts even without being busy. בעלי מומין have neither reason, so they make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: if he is busy with it, he is exempt even though it cannot be mixed up. If it can be mixed up, he is exempt even though he is not busy with it. This leaves out blemished animals, which cannot be mixed up and which he is not busy with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. He explains that רבי מאיר has two separate reasons for exempting, and either one alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf of שלמים is exempt because the person is busy offering it. חולין are exempt because they look just like a קרבן and can easily be mixed up. בעלי מומין are neither offered nor easily confused, so a person who slaughters them for a פסח is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
Can be confused
To exclude / to leave out
Blemished animals, which can never be offered

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a person who slaughters the wrong animal for a פסח is exempt if EITHER he was busy with a קרבן OR the animal could easily be mixed up. בעלי מומין fail both tests, so he is liable for them.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן answers רבא.

phrases.aramaic: טְרִיד — אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִחַלַּף,
phrases.english: If he is busy, he is exempt even though it cannot be confused,
phrases.notes: This is the calf of שלמים.

phrases.aramaic: מִחַלַּף — אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא טְרִיד,
phrases.english: if it can be confused, he is exempt even though he is not busy,
phrases.notes: This is חולין.

phrases.english: this excludes blemished animals,
which cannot be confused at all
and he is not busy with them at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טְרִיד — אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִחַלַּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two independent reasons: each one is enough to exempt on its own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר has only one reason, so the calf case and the חולין case contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being busy OR a possible mix-up is each enough to exempt. Only בעלי מומין, which have neither, make him liable.

steps.title: Eating נותר by mistake in place of roasted meat makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק sat on a porch and quoted רבי שמעון בן לקיש. If a spit of נותר was switched with a spit of roasted meat and a person ate it, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק were sitting on the porch of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק, and as they sat they said: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said, if a spit of נותר got switched for a spit of roasted meat and he ate it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a short story. Two אמוראים quote a ruling of רבי שמעון בן לקיש about a person who ate forbidden meat by mistake while trying to do a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating roasted קרבן meat is a מצוה, but eating נותר, meat left past its time, is forbidden. The person meant to do a מצוה and made a mistake. Even so, רבי שמעון בן לקיש says he is liable to bring a חטאת. Trying to do a מצוה does not protect him here.

keyTerms.meaning: On the porch / gateway area
A roasting spit
קרבן meat left past its allowed time, forbidden to eat
Roasted meat (here, permitted קרבן meat)
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new theme: what happens when someone makes a mistake while trying to do a מצוה. It connects to the earlier discussion about mistakes made with קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira sat
and Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak

phrases.aramaic: אַקִּילְעָא דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: on the porch of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak,
and they sat and were saying:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
If a spit of leftover (notar) meat got switched for him
with a spit of roasted meat,
and he ate it, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: mistakes made while trying to do a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who mistakenly ate נותר thinking it was permitted roasted קרבן meat is liable to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: liable with one's wife, exempt with one's יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules on relations with a נדה by mistake. A man who has relations with his wife who is a נדה is liable. A man who has relations with his יבמה who is a נדה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: if a man had relations with his wife who was a נדה, he is liable. If he had relations with his יבמה who was a נדה, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים quote a second ruling, this time from רבי יוחנן. He gives two cases with opposite results: liable with one's wife, exempt with one's יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a יבמה, the act of relations is itself the מצוה of יבום. So a mistake made while doing it counts as a mistake within a מצוה, and he is exempt. With his own wife, he is liable. This ruling seems to sit differently from רבי שמעון בן לקיש's ruling, which sets up the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state, forbidden in relations
Had relations
His brother's childless widow, whom he must marry through יבום
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the difference is about how bad the sin is. Both cases involve the same איסור of נדה. The only difference is that with a יבמה the act itself is a מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he had relations with his wife while she was a niddah, he is liable.
If he had relations with his yevamah while she was a niddah, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The relations are themselves the מצוה of יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה בָּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling quoted in the same conversation, on the same theme of mistakes made while doing a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with one's wife while she is a נדה make a man liable. Relations with one's יבמה while she is a נדה leave him exempt, because the act is the מצוה of יבום.

steps.title: First version: in the spit case he is surely liable
steps.stepSummary: One version says that רבי יוחנן would surely make him liable in the case of the switched spit of נותר, because there he did no מצוה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: all the more so, in that case (the switched spit) he is liable, because he did not do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רבי יוחנן's ruling about a wife who is a נדה to ריש לקיש's case of the switched spit. This first version says רבי יוחנן would agree that the person is liable there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן makes a man liable with his wife who is a נדה, even though he was doing a small מצוה. In the spit case he ate נותר, which is no מצוה at all. So if he is liable in the wife case, then all the more so he is liable in the spit case, which matches ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say. It introduces one version of a teaching.
All the more so. This is a קל וחומר style argument.
In that one. Here it means ריש לקיש's case of the switched spit.
Leftover קרבן meat that is forbidden to eat.

steps.confusionAlert: "That case" does not mean the יבמה. It points back to ריש לקיש's case from Step 17, where a spit of נותר was switched with a spit of roasted meat.

phrases.english: Some say:
all the more so in that case he is liable,
phrases.notes: "That case" is the switched spit of נותר (Step 17).

phrases.english: for he did not perform a מצוה.
phrases.notes: Eating נותר is not a מצוה. With his wife, he at least did a small מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּהָהִיא דְּמִחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's ruling (Step 18) to ריש לקיש's spit case (Step 17).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש that the person who ate the switched spit is liable, all the more so.

steps.title: Second version: in the spit case he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רבי יוחנן would exempt the person in the spit case. With his wife, he could have asked her. With the spit, there was no one to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: in that case (the spit) he is exempt. What is the reason? There (with his wife), he is liable because he should have asked her. But here (the spit), where he had no one to ask, he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite version of how רבי יוחנן would rule in the spit case. This version says he is exempt, and it gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for liability in the wife case is not about the מצוה. He is liable because he could have asked his wife whether she was a נדה, and he did not ask. In the spit case there was no one to ask, so he was not careless. According to this version, רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Others say. It introduces a second version.
Exempt, meaning he does not bring a חטאת.
What is the reason?
To ask, meaning to check before acting.

steps.whyThisMatters: This version gives a new reason for liability: a person is liable if he could have checked and did not. The question is not only whether he was doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: Others say: in that case, he is exempt.
What is the reason?
There (with his wife), it is because he should have asked.
phrases.notes: He could have asked his wife whether she was a נדה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְשַׁיּוֹלֵי — לָא.
phrases.english: But here (the spit), where he had no one to ask, he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version from Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, רבי יוחנן exempts the person in the spit case, because liability with his wife comes from failing to ask.

steps.title: Why is the יבמה different from the wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the יבמה case is exempt because he is doing a מצוה, then with his wife he is also doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, what is different about his יבמה? That he is doing a מצוה? With his wife he is also doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's split ruling from Step 18, where the wife case is liable and the יבמה case is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבמה case seems to be exempt because he is busy with the מצוה of יבום. But relations with his wife are also a מצוה, the מצוה of having children (פריה ורביה). So why is he not exempt in the wife case too?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
His brother's widow, whom he marries through יבום.
He is doing a מצוה.
His wife.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan, what is different about his yevama,
that he is doing a מצוה?
phrases.notes: The מצוה of יבום.

phrases.english: With his wife he is also doing a מצוה!
phrases.notes: The מצוה of פריה ורביה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 18 and questions the difference between the two cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's distinction between a wife who is a נדה (liable) and a יבמה who is a נדה (exempt).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases involve a מצוה, so the reason for exempting the יבמה should also exempt the wife.

steps.title: The wife is pregnant
steps.stepSummary: The wife case is about a pregnant wife, so the relations could not lead to having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where his wife is pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the wife case to a wife who is already pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is pregnant, the relations cannot fulfill the מצוה of having children. So in this case he is not doing that מצוה, and he is not exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Pregnant.
The מצוה to have children.

phrases.english: Where his wife is pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With his wife, he is always doing the מצוה of having children.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's wife case is about a pregnant wife, where the מצוה of having children does not apply.

steps.title: But there is still the מצוה of עונה
steps.stepSummary: Even with a pregnant wife, there is still the מצוה of שמחת עונה, so he is still doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still the מצוה of the joy of עונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 22. Even when she is pregnant, he still has a מצוה to give his wife her marital rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has a duty to be with his wife at set times (עונה), and this is itself a מצוה. So even with a pregnant wife he would be doing a מצוה. The difference between the wife and the יבמה is gone again.

keyTerms.meaning: The joy of marital relations that a husband owes his wife.
But there is! This phrase opens a challenge.

phrases.english: But there is the joy of conjugal rights!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a pregnant wife involves no מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצוה of עונה still applies to a pregnant wife, so he is still doing a מצוה.

steps.title: It was not the time of her עונה
steps.stepSummary: The case is when it was not her set time for עונה, so no מצוה was done at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is when it was not the time of her עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the wife case even more: it was not the time when he owed her relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the wife is pregnant, so there is no מצוה of having children. It is also not her set time, so there is no מצוה of עונה. With no מצוה at all, he is liable, unlike the יבמה case, where he does the מצוה of יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Not at the time of her עונה.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן makes a man liable with his wife who is a נדה only when he did no מצוה at all: she was pregnant and it was not her עונה. With a יבמה he is exempt because he does the מצוה of יבום.

phrases.english: Where it is not the time of her conjugal rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With a pregnant wife, the מצוה of עונה still applies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is when it was not her set time, so no מצוה was done, and he is liable.

steps.title: רבא's rule: pleasing one's wife is also a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. Even when it is not her עונה, רבא says a man must please his wife, so he was still doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: A person is obligated to make his wife happy through a matter of מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 24, which said that no מצוה was done because it was not her set time. It quotes רבא, who says that pleasing one's wife is a מצוה even outside her set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 tried to remove every מצוה from the wife case so that he would be liable there. רבא's rule shows that if the wife wants it, relations are still a מצוה even when it is not her עונה. So the wife case seems to go back to being a case of doing a מצוה, just like the יבמה case.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (so-and-so) say! This phrase opens a challenge from a known statement.
A leading אמורא of Babylonia
To make his wife happy, meaning to be with her when she desires it
An act that is a מצוה

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
A person is obligated to make his wife happy
phrases.notes: Even outside her regular עונה, when she shows desire.

phrases.english: through a matter of מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 24 that relations outside her עונה involve no מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא says that pleasing one's wife is itself a מצוה, so the wife case still involves a מצוה.

steps.title: The case was close to her expected period
steps.stepSummary: The case is when the relations happened near her וסת. At that time relations are forbidden, so there is no מצוה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was close to her expected time of her period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It sets the wife case at a time close to her וסת, when a husband must stay away from her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Near her וסת, relations are forbidden because she might become a נדה. That means no מצוה of pleasing her can apply at that time. Since this is his own wife, he also should have asked her about her timing, so he is not exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to, near
A woman's expected time for her period

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the relations were a weaker מצוה. The point is that at this time relations are forbidden, so there is no מצוה at all.

phrases.english: Close to her expected period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the wife case involved permitted relations, so the מצוה of pleasing her would apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The relations happened near her וסת, when they are forbidden, so there is no מצוה.

steps.title: Then the sister-in-law case should be liable too
steps.stepSummary: If being near her וסת makes him liable, then the יבמה could also have been near her וסת. So he should be liable there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with his יבמה he should also be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. It argues that the same reasoning should also apply to the יבמה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said that near her וסת relations are forbidden, so no מצוה applies. If so, relations with a יבמה near her וסת would also not be the מצוה of יבום. Then why would רבי יוחנן exempt him in the יבמה case and not in the wife case?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
His יבמה: his late brother's widow, whom he marries through יבום
Also

phrases.english: If so,
even his sister-in-law as well (he should be liable)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the wife case was near her וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same near-וסת issue could exist with the יבמה, so that case should also be liable.

steps.title: He is too shy to ask his sister-in-law
steps.stepSummary: He feels shy in front of his יבמה, so he could not ask her about her timing. He is not shy in front of his wife, so he should have asked her.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his יבמה, he is shy in front of her. With his wife, he is not shy in front of her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between the two cases. The difference is whether he could comfortably have asked her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife is familiar to him, so he could have asked if she was near her וסת. Since he did not ask, he is responsible for the mistake. The יבמה is new to him, so it is understandable that he did not ask. That is why he stays exempt in her case.

keyTerms.meaning: He is shy or embarrassed in front of her

steps.whatToRemember: The wife case is liable because the relations happened near her וסת, which removes any מצוה, and because he could have asked her. The יבמה case is exempt because he is doing a מצוה and was too shy to ask.

phrases.english: His sister-in-law: he is shy in front of her,
his wife: he is not shy in front of her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are the same, since either woman could be near her וסת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only with his wife could he have asked, so only there is he responsible.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רבי יוחנן follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier תנא supports רבי יוחנן's rule that a person who sins by mistake while doing a מצוה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, whose opinion does he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants to find the source in the משנה for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the cases are explained, the גמרא looks for a תנא who holds the same idea. The idea is that someone who made a mistake while busy with a מצוה does not bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whom? Whose opinion?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, in accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the cases to finding a source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא agrees with רבי יוחנן that a mistake made while doing a מצוה is exempt

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יוסי and the לולב on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי יוסי. He exempts someone who forgot it was שבת and carried a לולב into the public domain, because he carried it out with permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he follows רבי יוסי: As we learned in a משנה, רבי יוסי says: If the first day of סוכות falls on שבת, and a person forgot and carried the לולב into the public domain, he is exempt, because he carried it out with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, using the word אילימא ("if you say"). This word signals that the suggestion will probably be rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying on שבת is normally a sin that requires a חטאת. רבי יוסי exempts this person because he was busy with the מצוה of לולב. That looks just like רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. It introduces a suggestion that will likely be pushed away.
As we learned in a משנה
The palm branch taken on סוכות
The public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden
With permission, meaning while doing a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the wordplay. רשות הרבים means the public domain, while ברשות means with permission. They are two different ideas.

phrases.english: If you say like Rabbi Yosei.
As we learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
The first festival day of Sukkot
that falls on Shabbat,
and he forgot and carried out the lulav
into the public domain —
he is exempt,
because he carried it out with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of Step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן may follow רבי יוסי, who exempts someone who carried a לולב on שבת by mistake while busy with the מצוה.

steps.title: The לולב case is different because of time pressure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's case may be special. The לולב must be taken at a fixed time, so the person is rushed. יבום has no such time limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, since its time is pressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of לולב applies only on one set day, so a person is anxious and rushed to do it. That rush could explain why רבי יוסי exempts him. יבום can be done at any time, so רבי יוסי's reason may not cover רבי יוחנן's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
It is different there
Its time is pressing, so he is rushed

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the exemption for someone busy with a מצוה might depend on special conditions such as time pressure. If so, רבי יוחנן's broader rule still needs a source.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
since its time is pressing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in Step 30
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link between רבי יוחנן and רבי יוסי, not רבי יוחנן's rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's exemption may come from the time pressure of לולב. That pressure is missing with יבום.

steps.title: Suggesting רבי יהושע's ruling on offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהושע's ruling in our משנה about offerings slaughtered on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהושע in the case of offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from רבי יוסי failed. So the גמרא offers a new source: רבי יהושע in our משנה about זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, someone slaughtered a different animal on שבת by mistake, thinking it was a קרבן פסח. The animal was fit to be a פסח, and רבי יהושע exempts him from a חטאת. He made a mistake while busy with a מצוה, which sounds just like רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new attempt after the last one failed)
Offerings; here, the case in our משנה of slaughtering another offering as a פסח
The תנא who exempts in these cases

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves some words out; it means: maybe רבי יוחנן's source is רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: of the offerings case.
phrases.notes: Refers to our משנה (quoted in Step 5), where another offering fit to be a פסח was slaughtered on שבת for the sake of a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement source after the רבי יוסי proof was rejected in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע in the זבחים case of our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that טועה בדבר מצוה is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע in our משנה, who exempts someone who slaughtered another offering as a פסח on שבת.

steps.title: Offerings also have a pressing time
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In the offerings case the person was also rushed, because the פסח has a fixed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there too, his time was pressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from זבחים, using the same reason it used against רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח must be slaughtered on the afternoon of ערב פסח. Someone rushing to finish in time can be excused for a mistake. יבום has no deadline, so this case cannot prove רבי יוחנן's rule about יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (introduces a possible way out of a proof)
His time is pressing; the מצוה has a fixed time, so he is rushed
There too

steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say רבי יהושע disagrees with רבי יוחנן. It only says this case cannot prove the rule, because time pressure might be the real reason for the exemption.

phrases.english: Perhaps there too
phrases.notes: Like the לולב case of רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: his time is pressing.
phrases.notes: The פסח must be slaughtered at a fixed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects זבחים as a proof for רבי יוחנן's broad rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption may come from time pressure (זמנו בהול), which is missing in יבום.

steps.title: Suggesting רבי יהושע's ruling on babies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries another ruling of רבי יהושע: the case of two babies and a ברית מילה done on the wrong day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהושע in the case of the babies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third possible source: רבי יהושע's ruling about circumcising babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוהל had two babies. One was due for מילה on ערב שבת and one on שבת. He forgot and circumcised the ערב שבת baby on שבת. רבי יהושע exempts him from a חטאת. He broke שבת by mistake while busy with a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Babies; the case of two babies due for מילה on different days
Circumcision, which may be done on שבת when it falls on the eighth day

phrases.english: Rather, in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua
phrases.notes: Another attempt to find רבי יוחנן's source.

phrases.english: of the babies case.
phrases.notes: Two babies, one due for מילה on ערב שבת and one on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source after the זבחים proof was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע in the case of the babies.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that טועה בדבר מצוה is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's exemption for the מוהל who circumcised the wrong baby on שבת.

steps.title: Circumcision also has a pressing time
steps.stepSummary: Rejected again. מילה must be done on the eighth day, so the מוהל was rushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, his time is pressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the babies proof for the same reason as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה has a set day, the eighth day. That time pressure may be what excuses the mistake. So the case does not show that every טועה בדבר מצוה is exempt, and יבום has no set day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rushed, pressed

phrases.english: There too, his time is pressing.
phrases.notes: מילה has a fixed day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the babies case as a proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption may depend on the fixed time of מילה.

steps.title: Suggesting רבי יהושע's ruling on תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about a כהן who ate תרומה and then found out he was disqualified. רבי יהושע exempts him from paying קרן וחומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהושע about תרומה, as we learned: If someone was eating תרומה and it became known that he was a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, רבי אליעזר makes him pay the principal and a fifth, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a fourth attempt, this time with a case that seems to have no time pressure: eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man thought he was a כהן doing the מצוה of eating תרומה. Really he was a non-כהן eating תרומה by mistake, and such a person normally pays קרן וחומש. רבי יהושע exempts him, which looks just like רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion given to a כהן; only a כהן may eat it
Son of a כהן and a divorced woman; he is a חלל and may not eat תרומה
Son of a כהן and a woman who did חליצה; also disqualified
The principal plus an extra fifth, paid by a non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake
As we learned in a משנה
Exempts

phrases.english: Rather, in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua regarding terumah,
phrases.notes: A new attempt.

phrases.english: as we learned in a Mishnah:
If one was eating terumah
phrases.notes: He thought he was a כהן.

phrases.english: and it became known that he is the son of a divorcee
phrases.notes: So he is disqualified from כהונה.

phrases.english: or the son of a woman who did chalitzah —
phrases.notes: Also disqualified.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer obligates the principal and a fifth,
phrases.notes: Like any non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.
phrases.notes: This looks like support for רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two cases with time pressure failed, it picks a case that seems to have none.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע's exemption from קרן וחומש for a disqualified כהן who ate תרומה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that טועה בדבר מצוה is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות about a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה who ate תרומה.

steps.title: Even the תרומה case may involve time pressure
steps.stepSummary: Rejected. Following רב ביבי בר אביי, the case may be about חמץ תרומה on ערב פסח, which must be eaten quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it follows רב ביבי בר אביי, who said: it is talking about תרומה on ערב פסח, whose time is pressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects even the תרומה proof. It shows that this case can also be explained as one with time pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי בר אביי explains that the משנה is about תרומה that is חמץ, eaten on ערב פסח. If it is not eaten in time, it must be burned. So the person was rushed, and once again the case cannot prove a rule for יבום, which has no deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who places the תרומה case on ערב פסח
The day before פסח, when חמץ must be finished or burned by a set time
Whose time is pressing (said about the תרומה itself)

steps.whatToRemember: All four attempted sources (לולב, זבחים, תינוקות, תרומה) are rejected because each might involve a מצוה with a fixed time (זמנו בהול), and יבום has no such time limit. The next step adds a second, separate rejection for the תרומה case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key distinction. Exemption for a mistake made during a time-bound, rushed מצוה is narrower than רבי יוחנן's broad rule for any טועה בדבר מצוה.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is like Rav Beivai bar Abaye,
phrases.notes: Here comes an explanation that weakens the proof.

phrases.english: for Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
It is about terumah on the eve of Passover,
phrases.notes: תרומה that is חמץ.

phrases.english: whose time is pressing.
phrases.notes: It must be eaten before the time to burn חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תרומה proof of step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the תרומה case as a proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case may be set on ערב פסח, when the חמץ תרומה had to be eaten quickly, so time pressure explains the exemption.

steps.title: Second rejection: תרומה counts as service, and service is validated
steps.stepSummary: Another way to reject the proof from the תרומה case. Eating תרומה is called עבודה, and the Torah validates עבודה done by a כהן who turns out to be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: תרומה is different, because it is called 'service', and the Merciful One validated service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why the תרומה case from Step 36 cannot serve as a source for רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rejection (Step 37) said the כהן was rushed because of חמץ on ערב פסח. This rejection takes a new angle. Eating תרומה counts as עבודה, and the Torah has a special rule that accepts עבודה done by a כהן who later turns out to be disqualified. So רבי יהושע's exemption there may come from that special rule, not from a general principle about someone who made a mistake while doing a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another possible answer
It is different
Sacred service of a כהן
The Torah (the Merciful One) validated it

steps.confusionAlert: Step 37 already rejected this proof. This is not a continuation of that answer. It is a completely separate, second reason for the same rejection.

phrases.english: Alternatively: teruma is different,
because it is called service,
and service — the Merciful One validated it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: שָׁאנֵי תְּרוּמָה דְּאִיקְּרִי עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent rejection of the proof from Step 36, alongside Step 37.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the כהן who ate תרומה and was exempt from קרן וחומש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption may come from the special rule that validates עבודה, not from a general rule about a mistake made while doing a מצוה.

steps.title: Source that the Torah validates service by a disqualified כהן
steps.stepSummary: A משנה: a כהן who offered קרבנות and was found to be a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. רבי יהושע validates his offerings, based on ״ופועל ידיו תרצה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If a כהן was standing and offering, and it became known that he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, all the offerings he brought on the altar are disqualified. רבי יהושע validates them. We said: what is רבי יהושע's reason? As it is written: 'Bless, ה׳, his substance, and accept the work of his hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim it just made, that the Torah validates עבודה done by a disqualified כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן גרושה is a חלל and may not serve. Even so, רבי יהושע says his past offerings are valid after the fact. He learns this from the פסוק ״ופועל ידיו תרצה״‎: ה׳ accepts the work of the כהן's hands. This is the special rule that could also explain the תרומה case.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a divorced woman and a כהן; he is a חלל, unfit for כהונה
Son of a woman who had חליצה; also unfit for כהונה (Rabbinically)
Validates; rules it fit
'And accept the work of his hands' (דברים לג:יא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This source shows that רבי יהושע's leniency here is tied to a specific פסוק about עבודה. That is why the תרומה case cannot be stretched into a general rule.

phrases.english: As we learned: if he was standing and offering,
and it became known that he is the son of a divorcee
or the son of a woman who had ḥalitza —
all the offerings, every one that he offered
on top of the altar, are disqualified,
and Rabbi Yehoshua validates them.
And we said: what is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua?
As it is written: "Bless, Lord, his substance
and accept the work of his hands."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for 'עבודה רחמנא אכשר' from Step 38.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah validates, after the fact, עבודה done by a disqualified כהן (according to רבי יהושע).
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about a בן גרושה who offered קרבנות, and the פסוק ״ופועל ידיו תרצה״.

steps.title: Where is eating תרומה called service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that eating תרומה is called עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is תרומה called 'service'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the first half of Step 38's claim: what source calls eating תרומה a form of עבודה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ופועל ידיו תרצה' rule only helps if eating תרומה really counts as עבודה. Normally עבודה means the work in the בית המקדש, so the גמרא needs a source before it can apply the rule to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?
It is called

phrases.english: And where is teruma called service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption in Step 38 that תרומה is called עבודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that eating תרומה is considered עבודה.

steps.title: Story of רבי טרפון missing the study hall
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי טרפון missed the בית המדרש one evening. When רבן גמליאל asked why, he said he had been doing 'עבודה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: There was an incident with רבי טרפון, who did not come to the בית המדרש last night. In the morning רבן גמליאל found him and said: Why did you not come to the בית המדרש last night? He answered: I was performing service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering its question with a ברייתא. The story shows רבי טרפון calling something he did in the evening 'עבודה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון was a כהן. As the end of the story on the next amud shows, the 'עבודה' he did that evening was eating תרומה. So this story will be the source that eating תרומה is called עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a true story brought as a source
Last night; yesterday evening
Morning
I performed sacred service

phrases.english: As it was taught: an incident with Rabbi Tarfon
who did not come last night to the study hall.
In the morning Rabban Gamliel found him,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא בָּאתָ
phrases.english: and said to him: for what reason did you not come
last night to the study hall?
He said to him: I performed service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 40 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי טרפון called his evening activity, eating תרומה, 'עבודה'.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks how there can be service today
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבן גמליאל challenges רבי טרפון: how can there be עבודה today, with no בית המקדש? רבי טרפון begins to answer from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: All your words are astonishing! Where do we find service in our times? He said to him: Behold, the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, רבן גמליאל challenges רבי טרפון's claim, and רבי טרפון begins to answer. This line sets up the פסוק, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חורבן there are no קרבנות, so רבן גמליאל cannot see what 'עבודה' a כהן could do today. רבי טרפון's answer will be a פסוק showing that eating תרומה counts as עבודה even now. That פסוק will answer the גמרא's question from Step 40.

keyTerms.meaning: Astonishing, puzzling words
In our times, after the בית המקדש was destroyed
Behold, it (the פסוק) says

phrases.english: He said to him: all your words
are nothing but astonishing words;
service in this time — from where?
He said to him: behold it says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל דְּבָרֶיךָ אֵינָן אֶלָּא דִּבְרֵי תֵימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבן גמליאל's challenge to רבי טרפון's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's claim that he performed עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no בית המקדש today, so there should be no עבודה at all.
